$comment: When to put +typing on the wire, read by tests/shared/typing.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest. Both clients hold the same one number — when the last active went out, 0 for nothing outstanding — and ask this the same question.
$cases: `event` is what happened in the composer: typed (a keystroke with something left in the box), cleared (emptied by hand), sent. `send` is what goes on the wire, null for nothing. `nextLastActiveAt` is the state to hold until the next event.

cases.$comment: The first keystroke in a quiet composer. Nothing is outstanding, so this is the one that has to go.
cases.name: the first keystroke says active

cases.$comment: The spec's one hard rule: at most one active per three seconds.
cases.name: a keystroke inside the three seconds says nothing
exactly three seconds is still inside it
a keystroke after it renews the notice

cases.$comment: The phone used to run this on a timer rather than on keystrokes, so a half-written message left on screen told the channel you were typing for as long as it sat there. Nothing here fires without a keystroke; a receiver stops showing the notice after six seconds of silence, which says 'stopped' without spending a line.
cases.name: nothing is sent without a keystroke, however long the box sits
sending takes back the outstanding active

cases.$comment: The phone announced done twice for one message — once from the send, once from the box emptying behind it. The second had nothing left to take back.
cases.name: and the box emptying behind it says nothing more
emptying the box by hand takes it back too

cases.$comment: Saying you have stopped doing something you never said you were doing is noise, and on a network that counts lines it is noise with a cost.
cases.name: sending without ever having said active says nothing
